description: Concerted backside nucleophilic displacement of a leaving group on sp3 carbon via a trigonal bipyramidal transition state.
conditions: Strong unhindered nucleophile, polar aprotic solvent
major_product_rule: Nucleophile replaces leaving group with complete Walden inversion
selectivity_notes: Steric hindrance governs rate: Methyl > 1° > 2° >> 3° (unreactive)
stereochemistry_notes: 100% Inversion of stereochemical configuration at chiral carbon
source_reference: March's Advanced Organic Chemistry, 8th Ed., Ch. 10

description: Stepwise substitution proceeding via rate-determining ionization to form a planar sp2 carbocation intermediate followed by nucleophilic capture.
conditions: Weak neutral nucleophile, polar protic solvent
major_product_rule: Nucleophile captures carbocation at both faces
selectivity_notes: Carbocation stability governs rate: 3° > Allylic/Benzylic > 2° >> 1°
stereochemistry_notes: Racemization with slight excess of inversion due to ion-pair shielding
source_reference: Carey & Sundberg Advanced Organic Chemistry Part A, Ch. 4

description: Concerted elimination of beta-hydrogen and alpha-leaving group requiring anti-periplanar periplanar orbital alignment.
conditions: Strong base (e.g. NaOEt or t-BuOK), heat
major_product_rule: Small base yields Zaitsev (more substituted alkene); bulky base yields Hofmann alkene
selectivity_notes: Zaitsev rule dominates with small alkoxide bases
stereochemistry_notes: Strict anti-periplanar dihedral angle (180°) requirement
source_reference: March's Advanced Organic Chemistry, 8th Ed., Ch. 17

description: Stepwise elimination via rate-determining carbocation ionization followed by rapid deprotonation by weak base.
conditions: Non-nucleophilic strong acid or weak base, polar protic solvent, heat
major_product_rule: Thermodynamic Zaitsev (most substituted and E-configured alkene)
selectivity_notes: E-isomer preferred over Z-isomer to minimize A-1,3 strain
stereochemistry_notes: Non-stereospecific; thermodynamic alkene isomer controls outcome
source_reference: Carey & Sundberg Advanced Organic Chemistry Part A, Ch. 5

description: Stepwise elimination initiated by deprotonation alpha to an electron-withdrawing group forming a stabilized carbanion, followed by poor leaving group expulsion.
conditions: Base + poor leaving group (OH, F) adjacent to electron-withdrawing carbonyl
selectivity_notes: Requires acidic alpha-H and poor beta-leaving group
stereochemistry_notes: Yields conjugated (E)-alkene preferentially
source_reference: Smith, Organic Synthesis, 4th Ed., Ch. 2

description: Base-catalyzed enolate generation and nucleophilic addition to an aldehyde or ketone carbonyl yielding a beta-hydroxy carbonyl.
conditions: Dilute aqueous base (NaOH, KOH) or mild acid
selectivity_notes: Kinetic vs thermodynamic enolate controlled by temperature and base bulk
stereochemistry_notes: Zimmmerman-Traxler transition state controls syn/anti diastereoselectivity
source_reference: Strategic Applications of Named Reactions in Organic Synthesis, p. 8

description: Dehydration of aldol addition product via E1cB pathway yielding stable conjugated alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl.
conditions: Base or acid catalyst with heat
selectivity_notes: Driven by conjugation thermodynamic stability
stereochemistry_notes: Predominantly (E)-alkene isomer
source_reference: March's Advanced Organic Chemistry, 8th Ed., Ch. 16

description: Base-catalyzed condensation between two ester molecules possessing alpha-protons, yielding a beta-keto ester.
conditions: Strong non-nucleophilic alkoxide matching ester alkoxy group (e.g. NaOEt for ethyl ester)
selectivity_notes: Final irreversible deprotonation of beta-keto ester drives equilibrium to completion
stereochemistry_notes: Planar enolate intermediate
source_reference: Strategic Applications of Named Reactions, p. 86

description: Intramolecular Claisen condensation of a dicarboxylic ester leading to 5- or 6-membered cyclic beta-keto esters.
conditions: Matching sodium alkoxide base
selectivity_notes: Favors 5- and 6-membered rings due to low ring strain
stereochemistry_notes: Cis/trans bridgehead controlled by ring size thermodynamics
source_reference: Kürti & Czakó, Named Reactions in Organic Synthesis, p. 138

description: Nucleophilic 1,4-addition of a stabilized carbon enolate (Michael donor) to an activated alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl (Michael acceptor).
conditions: Catalytic base (piperidine, Et3N, NaOEt)
selectivity_notes: Soft nucleophiles favor soft beta-carbon (1,4-addition) over hard carbonyl carbon
stereochemistry_notes: Diastereoselectivity guided by enolate conformation and steric shielding
source_reference: March's Advanced Organic Chemistry, 8th Ed., Ch. 15

description: Base-induced hydride-transfer disproportionation of non-enolizable aldehydes yielding equimolar primary alcohol and carboxylic acid.
conditions: Concentrated strong hydroxide (50% aq NaOH or KOH)
major_product_rule: Equimolar primary alcohol and carboxylate salt
selectivity_notes: Only non-enolizable aldehydes (benzaldehyde, formaldehyde, pivalaldehyde)
stereochemistry_notes: Acyclic/achiral outcome
source_reference: Kürti & Czakó, Named Reactions, p. 74

description: Nucleophilic carbanion transfer from organomagnesium halide (RMgX) to carbonyl carbon followed by aqueous acid workup.
conditions: Anhydrous conditions under inert argon/N2, then mild aq. NH4Cl workup
major_product_rule: Formaldehyde -> 1° alcohol; Aldehydes -> 2° alcohol; Ketones -> 3° alcohol
selectivity_notes: Strictly incompatible with acidic protons (water, alcohols, terminal alkynes)
stereochemistry_notes: Cram / Felkin-Anh model predicts facial diastereoselectivity for chiral aldehydes
source_reference: March's Advanced Organic Chemistry, 8th Ed., Ch. 16

description: Two equivalents of Grignard reagent add sequentially to an ester via ketone intermediate, yielding symmetrical tertiary alcohol.
conditions: >= 2 equivalents RMgX in anhydrous ether, followed by aq NH4Cl workup
major_product_rule: Tertiary alcohol containing two identical R groups derived from Grignard reagent
selectivity_notes: Intermediate ketone is more reactive than starting ester and cannot be isolated
stereochemistry_notes: Achiral or racemic tertiary alcohol
source_reference: Carey & Sundberg Part B, Ch. 7

description: Acid-catalyzed condensation of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol proceeding via tetrahedral intermediate under Le Chatelier equilibrium.
conditions: Catalytic strong acid (H2SO4, p-TsOH), excess alcohol or Dean-Stark water removal
selectivity_notes: Steric crowding around alpha-carbon of carboxylic acid retards reaction rate
stereochemistry_notes: Configuration of chiral alcohol is retained (C-O bond of acid is broken)
source_reference: March's Advanced Organic Chemistry, 8th Ed., Ch. 16

description: Rapid nucleophilic acyl substitution of an acyl chloride with alcohol in the presence of pyridine or triethylamine.
conditions: Base scavenger (pyridine, DMAP, Et3N) to neutralize generated HCl
selectivity_notes: Acid chlorides are highly reactive and react cleanly without acid catalysis
stereochemistry_notes: Stereocenter on alcohol is 100% retained
source_reference: Smith, Organic Synthesis, 4th Ed., Ch. 3

description: Exothermic addition-elimination between acyl chloride and primary or secondary amine yielding an amide.
conditions: 2 equivalents amine (or 1 equiv amine + 1 equiv Et3N)
major_product_rule: Secondary or tertiary amide + amine hydrochloride
selectivity_notes: Primary and secondary amines react smoothly; tertiary amines do not form stable amides
stereochemistry_notes: Rigid planar amide bond with partial double bond character (trans preferred)
source_reference: Carey & Sundberg Part B, Ch. 3

description: Aromatic substitution by nitronium ion (NO2+) generated in situ from mixed nitric and sulfuric acids via Arenium ion (Wheland complex).
conditions: Concentrated HNO3 + concentrated H2SO4 (nitrating mixture)
selectivity_notes: EDG directs ortho/para; EWG directs meta and deactivates ring
stereochemistry_notes: Planar aromatic ring preserved
source_reference: March's Advanced Organic Chemistry, 8th Ed., Ch. 11

description: Bromination of aromatic ring catalyzed by Lewis acid (FeBr3 or AlBr3) via polarization of Br2.
conditions: Br2 with catalytic FeBr3 / AlBr3
selectivity_notes: Activating groups (OH, NH2, OMe) accelerate and direct ortho/para
stereochemistry_notes: Aromatic planarity restored upon proton loss from sigma complex
source_reference: Carey & Sundberg Part A, Ch. 10

description: Alkylation of aromatic ring by carbocation generated from alkyl halide and strong Lewis acid (AlCl3).
conditions: Alkyl halide + anhydrous AlCl3
selectivity_notes: Prone to polyalkylation and 1,2-hydride/alkyl skeletal rearrangements
stereochemistry_notes: Rearranged carbocation determines major product regiochemistry
source_reference: March's Advanced Organic Chemistry, 8th Ed., Ch. 11

description: Acylation of aromatic ring by resonance-stabilized acylium ion (R-C≡O+) avoiding rearrangement and polyalkylation.
conditions: Acyl chloride or anhydride + >1 equiv anhydrous AlCl3
selectivity_notes: No rearrangement occurs; deactivating carbonyl prevents polyacylation
stereochemistry_notes: Regiochemistry strictly ortho/para for activated substrates
source_reference: Strategic Applications of Named Reactions, p. 176

description: Coupling of an aldehyde or ketone with a triphenylphosphonium ylide via oxaphosphetane intermediate to form an alkene and Ph3P=O.
conditions: Phosphonium ylide generated with strong base (n-BuLi or NaH)
major_product_rule: Regiospecific alkene exactly at carbonyl position
selectivity_notes: Non-stabilized ylides yield (Z)-alkenes; stabilized ylides yield (E)-alkenes
stereochemistry_notes: Kinetic control gives Z-alkene; thermodynamic gives E-alkene
source_reference: Kürti & Czakó, Named Reactions, p. 488

description: Concerted suprafacial [4pi + 2pi] thermal cycloaddition between s-cis conjugated diene and dienophile creating a cyclohexene ring.
conditions: Thermal (heat) or Lewis acid catalysis (AlCl3, TiCl4)
selectivity_notes: Endo rule governs kinetic product due to secondary orbital interaction
stereochemistry_notes: Strictly stereospecific suprafacial-suprafacial addition
source_reference: Woodward & Hoffmann, Conservation of Orbital Symmetry, Ch. 6

description: Peroxyacid-mediated oxidative cleavage of ketones into esters (or cyclic ketones into lactones) via Criegee intermediate.
conditions: mCPBA or trifluoroperacetic acid (TFPAA) with buffer (NaHCO3)
major_product_rule: Ester or lactone with oxygen inserted adjacent to more substituted carbon
selectivity_notes: Migratory aptitude: 3° alkyl > cyclohexyl > 2° alkyl ~ benzyl > phenyl > 1° alkyl > methyl
stereochemistry_notes: Retention of configuration at migrating stereocenter
source_reference: Strategic Applications of Named Reactions, p. 28

description: Acid-catalyzed rearrangement of ketoximes to substituted amides via anti-periplanar migration to electron-deficient nitrogen.
conditions: Protic acid (H2SO4, PPA) or Lewis acid (SOCl2, PCl5)
major_product_rule: Substituted amide or lactone (cyclic oxime -> lactam)
selectivity_notes: Strict migration of the group positioned anti to the oxime hydroxyl group
stereochemistry_notes: Intramolecular concerted migration with complete retention of migrating carbon configuration
source_reference: Kürti & Czakó, Named Reactions, p. 44

description: Acid-catalyzed dehydration and 1,2-alkyl or aryl shift of vicinal diols to give carbonyl compounds.
conditions: Concentrated H2SO4 or TsOH with heat
selectivity_notes: Protonation occurs at OH yielding more stable carbocation; aryl groups migrate faster than alkyl
stereochemistry_notes: Inversion at migration terminus, retention at migrating group
source_reference: March's Advanced Organic Chemistry, 8th Ed., Ch. 18

description: Mild, chemoselective reduction of aldehydes and ketones to primary and secondary alcohols respectively.
conditions: NaBH4 in protic solvent
major_product_rule: Aldehyde -> Primary Alcohol; Ketone -> Secondary Alcohol
selectivity_notes: Chemoselective: Does not reduce esters, amides, or carboxylic acids
stereochemistry_notes: Hydride delivery from less hindered face (Felkin-Anh control)
source_reference: March's Advanced Organic Chemistry, 8th Ed., Ch. 19

reaction_name: Lithium Aluminium Hydride Reduction of Esters
description: Powerful nucleophilic hydride reduction of esters to two primary alcohols via aldehyde intermediate.
conditions: Anhydrous LiAlH4 under argon, followed by Fieser workup
major_product_rule: Primary alcohol (from acyl portion) + alcohol (from alkoxy portion)
selectivity_notes: Reduces esters, carboxylic acids, amides, aldehydes, ketones
stereochemistry_notes: Achiral primary alcohol outcome
source_reference: Carey & Sundberg Part B, Ch. 5

description: Mild, anhydrous oxidation of primary alcohols to aldehydes (avoiding over-oxidation) and secondary alcohols to ketones.
conditions: Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) in anhydrous organic solvent
selectivity_notes: Absence of water prevents gem-diol formation and over-oxidation to carboxylic acid
stereochemistry_notes: Planar sp2 carbonyl created
source_reference: Strategic Applications of Named Reactions, p. 118

description: Concerted electrophilic oxygen transfer from peroxycarboxylic acid (mCPBA) to alkene forming an oxirane ring with syn stereospecificity.
conditions: mCPBA (meta-chloroperbenzoic acid) + solid NaHCO3 buffer
selectivity_notes: Electron-rich, more substituted alkenes react significantly faster
stereochemistry_notes: 100% stereospecific syn-addition: cis-alkene gives cis-epoxide; trans-alkene gives trans-epoxide
source_reference: March's Advanced Organic Chemistry, 8th Ed., Ch. 15

description: Concerted syn-addition of borane (BH3·THF) across an alkene followed by alkaline peroxide oxidation yielding anti-Markovnikov alcohol.
conditions: 1. BH3:THF complex (syn-addition); 2. H2O2, aq NaOH (oxidation)
selectivity_notes: Boron attaches to less hindered, less substituted alkene carbon
stereochemistry_notes: Stereospecific syn-addition of H and OH with retention of configuration during oxidation
source_reference: Carey & Sundberg Part B, Ch. 4

description: Electrophilic addition of mercuric acetate across alkene forming cyclic mercurinium ion, water attack, and NaBH4 demercuration.
conditions: 1. Hg(OAc)2 in H2O/THF; 2. NaBH4, aq NaOH
selectivity_notes: Nucleophile attacks more substituted carbon of mercurinium ion
stereochemistry_notes: Anti-addition of Hg and OH in step 1; demercuration is non-stereospecific
source_reference: March's Advanced Organic Chemistry, 8th Ed., Ch. 15

description: Heterogeneous syn-addition of molecular hydrogen across a pi bond over metal catalyst (Pd/C, PtO2, Raney Ni).
conditions: H2 gas (1-3 atm) over 5-10% Pd on activated charcoal
selectivity_notes: Alkenes reduce faster than carbonyls and aromatic rings
stereochemistry_notes: 100% syn-addition of two hydrogen atoms from catalyst surface
source_reference: Smith, Organic Synthesis, 4th Ed., Ch. 4

description: Reaction of primary aromatic amine with nitrous acid (NaNO2 + HCl) at low temperature to generate an arenediazonium salt.
conditions: NaNO2 + conc. HCl, ice bath (0-5°C to avoid thermal decomposition)
selectivity_notes: Strict temperature control <= 5°C required; forms versatile synthetic intermediate
stereochemistry_notes: Planar aromatic diazonium cation
source_reference: March's Advanced Organic Chemistry, 8th Ed., Ch. 13

description: Copper(I)-catalyzed replacement of diazonium group in arenediazonium salts with Cl, Br, or CN.
conditions: Copper(I) halide (CuCl or CuBr) or CuCN
major_product_rule: Aryl halide (Ar-Cl, Ar-Br) or aryl nitrile (Ar-CN) + N2 gas
selectivity_notes: Proceeds via single-electron transfer (SET) aryl radical pathway
stereochemistry_notes: Planar aromatic ring preserved
source_reference: Strategic Applications of Named Reactions, p. 394

description: Weak-base catalyzed condensation of an active methylene compound (malonate, cyanoacetate) with an aldehyde or ketone followed by dehydration.
conditions: Weak amine base catalyst (piperidine / beta-alanine) with acetic acid
selectivity_notes: Active methylene (pKa < 13) reacts selectively without self-condensation of aldehyde
stereochemistry_notes: Predominantly (E)-geometry of conjugated alkene
source_reference: Kürti & Czakó, Named Reactions, p. 248
